title: Get started with CellSight
text: Every CellSight app built two steps, order: makeShinyFiles() reads object writes app’s data shiny.dir — chunked HDF5 expression matrices plus .rds files holding config cell metadata, prefixed shiny.prefix (sc1 default). makeShinyCodes() writes app’s code directory — server.R, ui.R shinyFunc.R. split matters data step slow one, prefix ties two together. Whatever pass shiny.prefix makeShinyFiles() must passed makeShinyCodes().

title: Get started with CellSight
text: Using multimodal PBMC CITE-seq object (162,000 cells, 228 antibodies): leaves complete app shinyApp/. Open shinyApp/ui.R RStudio click Run App, console: See vignette("deployment") hosting somewhere laptop.
code: library(Seurat) library(cellsight)  seu <- readRDS("multimodal_pbmc.rds")  scConf <- createConfig(seu)  makeShinyFiles(seu, scConf, shiny.prefix = "sc1", shiny.dir = "shinyApp/")  makeShinyCodes(   shiny.title  = "PBMC multiomics",   shiny.prefix = "sc1",   shiny.dir    = "shinyApp/" ) shiny::runApp("shinyApp")

title: Get started with CellSight
text: createConfig() inspects object’s cell metadata returns data.table — conventionally called scConf — one row per metadata column expose app. decides columns usable, picks colour palette categorical one, guesses two shown default. usually want adjust : rename metadata display, drop uninteresting columns, fix colours. mod* helpers , worth build — see vignette("configuration"). Two arguments worth knowing front: createConfig() errors finds multi-level metadata , since app nothing group cells empty. hit , object probably clustered yet. building, check config still matches object:
code: scConf <- createConfig(seu) showOrder(scConf) # Only expose specific metadata columns scConf <- createConfig(seu, meta.to.include = c("orig.ident", "seurat_clusters", "celltype"))  # Allow more categories per metadata column (default 50; anything above is dropped) scConf <- createConfig(seu, maxLevels = 100) checkConfig(scConf, seu)

Two functions let look edit: showLegend() fastest way catch palette reads badly, takes fontSize labels long.
code: showOrder(scConf)    # a data.frame of ID / UI / levels, in display order showLegend(scConf)   # a ggplot of every legend, with its colours

title: Configuring metadata and colours
text: Restrict creation time already know want: start everything prune. delMeta() takes vector: addMeta() brings column back, adds one createConfig() skipped — note needs object , since read column’s levels: maxLevels guard accidentally exposing something like per-cell barcode categorical variable; raise deliberately.
code: scConf <- createConfig(seu, meta.to.include = c("orig.ident", "seurat_clusters", "celltype")) scConf <- delMeta(scConf, c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt")) scConf <- addMeta(scConf, "Phase", seu) scConf <- addMeta(scConf, c("donor", "timepoint"), seu, maxLevels = 100)

title: Configuring metadata and colours
text: modMetaName() changes app-facing label, never underlying column, vectorised: modLabels() renames levels within one metadata. Unlike others takes exactly one metadata time, new.labels must order existing levels — check showOrder() first:
code: scConf <- modMetaName(   scConf,   meta.to.mod = c("orig.ident", "seurat_clusters", "percent.mt"),   new.name    = c("Library", "Cluster", "% mitochondrial") ) showOrder(scConf)  scConf <- modLabels(   scConf,   meta.to.mod = "Cluster",   new.labels  = c("Naive CD4 T", "Memory CD4 T", "CD14 Mono", "B", "NK") )

title: Configuring metadata and colours
text: modColours() also takes one metadata time, one colour per level level order. format R accepts works — hex codes named colours: Colour palettes good place deliberate: default colorRampPalette() interpolation 12-colour Paired-style set, starts produce near-indistinguishable neighbours metadata roughly dozen levels. cluster label matters, give colour survives one point among 100,000. sequential colourblind-safe set, generate rather hand-pick:
code: scConf <- modColours(   scConf,   meta.to.mod = "Cluster",   new.colours = c("#4E79A7", "#F28E2B", "#E15759", "#76B7B2", "#59A14F") ) # "Cluster" here is the display name (UI); use the object's column name if you # have not renamed it. modColours() errors unless the lengths match exactly. n <- length(strsplit(scConf[UI == "Cluster"]$fID, "\\|")[[1]]) scConf <- modColours(scConf, "Cluster", scales::hue_pal()(n))

title: Configuring metadata and colours
text: reorderMeta() sets order metadata appear app’s dropdowns. Unlike helpers accepts ID values — object’s column names, display names — needs complete permutation: every ID present exactly , errors. code: scConf$ID #> [1] "orig.ident" "seurat_clusters" "celltype" "Phase"  scConf <- reorderMeta(scConf, c("celltype", "seurat_clusters", "orig.ident", "Phase"))

title: Configuring metadata and colours
text: Putting together, typical config pass looks like: build, vignette("cellsight").
code: scConf <- createConfig(seu) scConf <- delMeta(scConf, c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt")) scConf <- modMetaName(scConf, c("orig.ident", "seurat_clusters"), c("Library", "Cluster"))  # one colour per level, in level order nClust <- length(strsplit(scConf[UI == "Cluster"]$fID, "\\|")[[1]]) scConf <- modColours(scConf, "Cluster", scales::hue_pal()(nClust))  # reorderMeta() wants IDs, and all of them scConf <- reorderMeta(scConf, c("celltype", "seurat_clusters", "orig.ident")) scConf <- modDefault(scConf, "celltype", "Cluster")  checkConfig(scConf, seu) showLegend(scConf)
